clue.text: Salad vegetable right with a serving of food

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written
a dish is a portion of food served at a meal

explanation.surface: A salad vegetable sits on the right of a plate alongside a helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective for the serving, but it is just the abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red root with a peppery bite, commonly sliced raw into green salads.

clue.text: Love party to occupy most of region

indicators.note: most but not all of a word means its final letter is lost
to occupy a space is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: AREA, a region, without its last letter
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Revellers in love plan a party that will take over most of a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' could be zero in tennis, but here it is the verb defining the answer, and region needs a synonym before anything is trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as verbs, both mean to feel deep affection or devotion toward someone.

clue.text: Leading popular promenade

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
the front is the seaside promenade, as in the sea front

explanation.surface: A well-liked walkway by the sea heads the list.
explanation.walkthrough: In British seaside towns the front is the promenade along the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who is ahead of the field is in the lead, positioned ahead of all rivals.

clue.text: Sexy husband on bed, topless

indicators.note: without a top, a word loses its first letter
in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
COT, a small bed, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a shirtless husband lounging on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' fits the risqué picture, but it only strips the first letter from the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, someone hot is physically attractive and arousing desire.

clue.text: Father embracing a deity in eastern temple

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A father worships a god inside a temple in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-letter word for father is split open so that the next three words fit between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine across Asia is the classic example.

clue.text: Law has intellectual property left in control of royalty

indicators.note: something in the control of another is held within its grasp, so it goes inside

parts.note: a prince is a member of a royal family
IP is the usual abbreviation for intellectual property
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A legal ruling says patents and copyrights are left in the hands of the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royalty' suggests payments earned from intellectual property, but it means a royal person, who holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental rule or truth, such as a scientific law, is a basic tenet from which others follow.

clue.text: Range that's good with a stomach being upset

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A wide selection of food that's fine even with an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset stomach' reads as indigestion; here it means A and TUM get shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole gamut is the complete spectrum or scope of something, such as emotions or notes.

clue.text: Finished entertainment in December, heading for theatre

indicators.note: something in another is placed inside it, so one piece goes within

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
fun is amusement or entertainment

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, at the top

parts.note: the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: A December show has ended, and everyone heads to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Month abbreviations are standard in crosswords; the entertainment is plain fun, sitting inside the month before the theatre's initial is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct no longer exists or functions, like a business that has closed down.

clue.text: Scattered pieces of paper etc? Not if tidied up

indicators.note: tidying up moves things into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bits of paper lie everywhere, unless someone sweeps them up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'etc' look like part of the definition; ETC is anagram fodder. The joke is that tidying confetti would leave it no longer scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coloured paper shreds are thrown over newlyweds at weddings and at celebrations.

clue.text: Bungle in leaving cake

indicators.note: when letters leave a word they are taken away from it

parts.note: a muffin is a small cake
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mess of getting out of a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN out of MUFFIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To muff a catch or a chance is to handle it clumsily and fail, a casual verb for blundering.

clue.text: Nothing runs, nothing, after size reduced by 50 per cent

indicators.note: cutting something by half removes half of its letters
one piece placed after another follows it in the order

parts.note: the second half of the word size
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O looks like a nought

explanation.surface: A cricket report: no runs, nothing at all, after a team was cut down to half its size.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Nothing' is the definition; the second gives the O. In cricket scoring, R stands for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The number written as nought represents an empty quantity, none at all.

clue.text: Dramatic departure involving leader of Conservatives

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: exiting is the act of leaving

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Conservatives

explanation.surface: A politician storms out in a scene that drags in the head of the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits inside EXITING, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe events that are thrilling and full of excitement, stirring strong feeling.

clue.text: Ruling out our group in revised lexicon

indicators.note: putting something in and then revising the whole means the combined letters get reworked

parts.note: us is the speaker's own group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new dictionary edition leaves our group's words out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' is a noun-verb phrase: the definition is the gerund 'ruling out', matching a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of deciding that something is not allowed or not included is a refusal to admit it.

clue.text: Cold aboard lorry, very cold

indicators.note: to be aboard a vehicle is to be inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A refrigerated truck carries chilled cargo in freezing temperatures.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is a British truck, and an artic is a big articulated one with a hinged trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar conditions near the North Pole give the adjective its sense of freezing weather.

clue.text: New record regarding rental agreement

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a lease is a contract for renting property

explanation.surface: A fresh entry is logged about a tenancy contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a document filed about the lease, but it is a music recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A band's latest album or single, put out for sale, is called its latest issue.

clue.text: Vegetable placed in stewpot at once

indicators.note: something placed in a phrase sits within its run of letters

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A vegetable is dropped into the stew pot straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed in' reads as cooking instructions, but it points to letters sitting inside the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy tuber that is a staple in kitchens worldwide, often boiled for stews.

clue.text: Tot's first tucking into light brown liquor? Childish rage

indicators.note: tucking something into another puts it inside

parts.note: tan is a light yellowish-brown

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of tot
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A toddler gets into the rum and throws a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light brown liquor' reads as one drink, but it splits into a colour and a spirit. A tot is also a small measure of spirits, which suits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncontrolled outburst of anger, typical of a small child, is the classic example.

clue.text: Certain to get behind request for amusement

indicators.note: to be behind something is to follow it, so this piece comes second

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to back a request for some entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get behind' suggests support for the request; in the wordplay it means placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or delight taken in something fun is what both words describe.

clue.text: Change promotional material, appending a point

indicators.note: to append is to attach at the end, so this piece follows

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
taken as written
PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: An editor revises an advert by adding one more selling point.
explanation.walkthrough: PT is the standard abbreviation for point, as in a type size.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something so it suits a new purpose or situation is to alter it.

clue.text: What thief will do in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to steal, in British slang
second meaning: British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: What a burglar ends up doing behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: to nick is to steal, and the nick is jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pinch or steal something, and the noun is informal for a lock-up or police cells.

clue.text: Opening for college girl in group of students

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of college
a lass is a girl, mainly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A college has a place for a young woman in its student group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a vacancy at the college; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils taught together in one school year or course form a single teaching set.

clue.text: Programmer's favourite source of coffee?

parts.note: surface reading: where a coder likes to get a caffeine fix
setter's reading: a well-known programming language that shares its name with an Indonesian coffee-growing island

explanation.walkthrough: The word names an island in Indonesia famous for coffee, slang for coffee itself, and a widely used programming language.
explanation.definitionFit: The island grows coffee beans, the word is American slang for a cup of coffee, and coders write in the language.

clue.text: I travel freely after November period

indicators.note: one piece after another follows it in sequence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: moving freely means without fixed order, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone plans to roam at will once November's term is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters follow N, while I stays at the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time between two events, or a break in a show, is a span of time.

clue.text: Bathroom item with short pipe

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: TUBE, a pipe, without its final letter

explanation.surface: A bath fitting supplied with a stubby length of plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short pipe' sounds like a plumbing part, but 'short' trims the last letter from the word for a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is the large basin a person lies in to wash, a standard bathroom fixture.

clue.text: Silent film star ruined no take

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A silent-era actor spoils a scene, so the director gets no usable take.
explanation.walkthrough: Buster Keaton was a deadpan comic actor of the silent era, famed for stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster of that surname was one of the great comedians of silent cinema in the 1920s.

clue.text: Puzzle to act as inspiration?

parts.note: to be something is to serve in that role
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A setter wonders whether a crossword can spark creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or confuse someone is to leave them baffled and perplexed.
